evals.prompt: Delegate five independent read-only repository reviews to OpenCode and Antigravity in parallel. Keep each workspace and session identifiable, do not use a scheduler, and return whenever any one task finishes so you can review it before waiting again.
evals.expected_output: Loads the implementer-specific delegate skills, uses a durable supervisor with distinct output directories, and waits through watch-once using a sequence cursor.

evals.prompt: Continue the failed OpenCode subagent task from yesterday in the same repository and let me watch its tool actions in a separate terminal window.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the canonical workspace identity, resumes only the requested session, and opens the human timeline viewer without stopping or duplicating the task.

evals.prompt: Have three agents implement independent changes at the same time in Sanad, and keep their edits from colliding.
evals.expected_output: Requires isolated worktrees and separate sessions/conversations, bounds concurrency, and preserves the no-commit/no-push boundary unless separately authorized.

evals.prompt: Ask OpenCode one quick read-only question and wait for the answer in this terminal.
evals.expected_output: Uses opencode-delegate directly because durable multi-task supervision adds no value to a short one-off foreground request.
